title: Noise-adaptive paging policy with silent failover and runbook automation
creator: Liam O'Connor
description: Design and implement a noise-adaptive paging policy that reduces alert fatigue by probabilistically suppressing noisy signals, performs a silent failover to a warm standby region when degradation is persistent, and wires automated runbook steps (context enrichment, remediation attempts, and escalation) into the on-call workflow. The goal is to reduce false positives, improve mean time to mitigation for true incidents, and keep user-visible impact minimal during transient infra noise.
acceptance_criteria: Paging rate reduced by >=40% for alerts identified as noise in the experimental cohort without increasing time to acknowledge for real degradations
Silent failover triggers only when composite degraded signal persists for 90s and circuit breaker score >=0.8, with telemetry showing <1% additional error surface post-failover

Automated runbook executes prerequisite context enrichment (last 5 minutes of traces, top 3 callers, recent deploys), attempts two non-intrusive remediations, and either resolves the incident or escalates according to policy
Playbook and automation covered by unit/integration tests and e2e incident simulation in the staging multiregion environment
Runbook steps surface in Console incident view and include links to PRs, dashboards, and postmortem template
tasks: Define probabilistic suppression model and feature set (rate, co-occurrence, historical noisiness)
Implement alert scoring pipeline (ingest -> enrich -> score) in monitoring stack
Add circuit breaker scoring and threshold config to routing layer
Build silent failover orchestration with rollback hooks and canary verification
Author runbook templates and map automation steps to on-call approvals
Integrate with Pager and Console UI for suppressed alert visibility
Create incident simulation harness and run 5 experiments in staging
Write tests and update SLO dashboards to reflect new failover events
implementation_notes: We'll compute a per-alert noise score using features: recent flapping frequency, historical actioned_ratio, temporal correlation with deploys, and downstream error correlation
Suppression is probabilistic: alerts with score in [0.6,0.85) are sampled with a decreasing probability; score >=0.85 triggers automated mitigation workflow but is not paged directly
Circuit breaker score aggregates regional tokenized latency percentiles, error budget burn rate, and infra saturation metrics; score range normalized to [0,1]
Silent failover uses warm standby routing with traffic ramp over 30s and active canary checks (synthetic requests) for quick rollback
Automation will use existing runbook execution service; non-intrusive remediations include cache flush and rolling restart of a non-critical worker pool
All automated remediation attempts require a 1-click on-call confirmation for escalations beyond two attempts
testing_plan: Unit tests for alert scoring function and probability sampler
Simulated alert burst replay with injected noise traces to validate suppression recall/precision
Staging multiregion chaos run: induce region A latency spike and verify silent failover execution and rollback
On-call tabletop with SREs and Engineering to validate runbook clarity and timing
A/B experiment in production for 2% of accounts to measure paging reduction and MTTD/MTTR changes
rollback_plan: Disable suppression and silent failover feature flags; if regressions observed, immediately switch routing back to primary region and run emergency remediations. Post-rollback, capture incident data and revert model changes. Owners: Aisha Patel (SRE), Ethan Zhang (Serving Runtime).
